translations.text: The names of the sons of Israel were written on these shoulder-pieces, because the twelve names could not have been written together on a single emerald stone. Instead they were divided:
six tribes were written on one stone and six on the other.
The six tribes for the blessing on Gerizim were written on the stone that was on the right shoulder-piece, and the six tribes for the curse on Ebal were written
on the stone that was on the left shoulder-piece. These mountains are opposite Jericho, on the east side, near Gilgal.
The books tell us this about the place where the sons of Israel were blessed. Those who were on Mount Gerizim and spoke the blessings were:
Simeon, Levi, Judah and the other three with them. They spoke thus: "Blessed is he who does the will of the Lord."
And the sound of the response could be heard in the plains where the people stood. And they said: "So be it! So be it!"
And then Reuben, Gad, Asher and Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali were on Mount Ebal, and they spoke thus: "Cursed be everyone who does not do what is written in these books of the law!"
And all the people say: "So be it! So be it!" And "Amen" is translated "So be it."
For the voice from the two mountains and the response of the two companies could be heard by the people who stood in the plain between the two mountains.
And in translation Mount Gerizim is called "mountain of deliverance," and Mount Ebal "defiled and polluted."
But some people, who have read the divine books without understanding, think otherwise, above all the race of the Samaritans:
they say that Mount Gerizim is something else, namely the high mountain that rises above Sikima, which is Shechem, the mountain that is opposite Shechem, the city of the Samaritans.
This is the city the Lord entered, and from it the Samaritan woman came out and saw the Lord, for he was sitting by the well.
And Shechem is now called Neapolis. It is a rich and populous city in the land of the Palestinians, and at that time Samaritans and Jews lived in it.
And they are called Samaritans because the mountain near that city was called the mountain of Somer, and he had a son and called his name Someron.
The mountain too was given the name Somer. Because of this the race of the Samaritans received its name.
And the race of the Samaritans came from the land of the Babylonians and the Assyrians.
Nebuchadnezzar had brought them and settled them in the land of the Galileans and the Palestinians.
When Nebuchadnezzar took the sons of Israel captive, the elders of the sons of Israel went in before King Nebuchadnezzar.
And the men who went in before King Nebuchadnezzar were Ezra, others from among the priests, and elders of the sons of Israel.
And they begged Nebuchadnezzar to send men to guard their land, so that the land would not turn into forest and be overthrown and ruined.
And Nebuchadnezzar heard their request. He chose his own servants from four peoples and sent them to guard their land.
And these were the names of the peoples who went to settle in the land of Israel: the Kudaeans, the Cuthaeans, the Sepharvaeans and the Anagonaeans.
And each of these peoples had its own idols, which they worshipped and called gods. They came and settled near Mount Somer.
